chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever makes a will but does not guard it properly and is not harmed [by the heirs' actions], is like one who gave it in charity during his lifetime."

key_terms.يُضَارَّ: to be harmed or suffer detriment

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a will if the heirs execute it without causing harm?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a will executed by heirs, equating it to the testator's own voluntary charity (sadaqah) provided no harm (darar) or injustice occurs. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the testator's reward through the heirs' faithful execution, linking the concept of bequest closely to the spiritual merit of almsgiving during one's lifetime.
